title: R' Yosi Ketanta
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Mishnah Sotah, chapter 9, mishnah 15](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Sotah.9.15): when he died, the pious ceased. Why was he called Ketanta? Because he was the “small one” among the pious. In the Gemara there he is called Abba Yosi ben Ketunta. The Yerushalmi reads “Yosi ben Ketunta, who was the epitome of the pious,” and says: “When Rabbi Yosi Hasida and Rabbi Yosi Ketunta died, men of piety ceased.” From this we see that Rabbi Yosi Hasida is not Rabbi Yosi Ketunta; see the entry Isi ben Yehudah.[^1]

notes.text: The supplied source already corrects an ambiguous printed word to תמציתן, rendered “epitome.” The frozen Guggenheimer, Mechon-Mamre and Venice texts of [Yerushalmi Sotah 9:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.9.16) support תמציתן של חסידים in the Mishnah clause. This supports the source’s explicit editorial correction; it does not establish that every printed glyph reads that way. The later discussion has תמציתן/תמציתו variants, which are not conflated. The earlier English note saying no witness was supplied is now superseded. The forms קטנתא and קטונתא in Hyman, and קיטונתא in the parallel, are spelling variants kept distinct; “small one” is a literal rendering of Hyman’s first explanation. The final distinction between the two Yosi figures is Hyman’s inference, not a new identity binding. His [Mishnah 9:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Sotah.9.15) and “Gemara there” labels are retained without adding an unprinted Bavli daf.

The heading retains Hyman’s abbreviated title as R'. The full titles in the quoted Yerushalmi passage follow Guggenheimer’s רִבִּי יוֹסֵי חֲסִידָא וְרִבִּי יוֹסֵי קָטוֹנְתָא. This supports those occurrences without settling a general identity for every similarly named figure.
